Names in this guide: `subagent` is `Agent`, `skill` is `Skill`, and `mcp__papermemory__*` is `mcp__plugin_academic-harness_papermemory__*`. If a tool named below is not in your tool list, say so.

## Academic Harness (LaTeX papers, grants, theses)

When the working directory is an Academic Harness project (`ah.yaml` present), or the user asks to start, audit, plan, write, or fix a literature review, journal/conference paper, grant, thesis, or rebuttal in LaTeX, load `academic-harness` (router) or the matching `ah-write-unit` / `ah-plan-section` / `ah-draft-from-plan` / `ah-fix-findings` / `ah-audit-section` / `ah-revise-from-review`.

This is the writing oracle: coverage of every number, cite, unit and declared claim (`ah_inventory`), plus a gate that closes only when this turn introduced no open blocker or major. It does not mean the science is true.

- Use the `ah_*` tools. Do not `pip install academic-harness` and do not install it separately; the engine is vendored inside this plugin (`vendor/academic-harness`). Override with `ACADEMIC_HARNESS_CLI` or `AH_CMD`. Do not shell out to `ah` when a native tool exists.
- The harness injects a paper-state card, blocks writes to sources/facts/ledger/briefs/plans/outline, re-checks after each prose edit, and will not let you stop while your edits introduced blocking findings (then hands off: report them and wait).
- Register evidence with `ah_source` `add` before citing it; look up passages with `ah_source_search`. `ah_units` syncs anchors; `ah_fact` `build` rebuilds macros. After a value or term changes, `ah_sweep`.
- Numbers from project data: `\fact{id}` (`ah_fact` lists ids). Cite only registered sources. Keep every `%% @unit` line with its paragraph.
- `ah_done` answers whether the document as a whole is done: pass, fail or incomplete, with the deciding component named (findings at a blocking level, open findings from admitted rubric criteria, stale or missing external results, findings with no cause, a registry snapshot older than the limit). Incomplete is not a pass: something that matters was not looked at. It says nothing about whether the science is sound.
- Free reviews (`deep_review`, `peer-reviewer`, `pre-submission-reviewer`) are exploratory and never gating: they raise different points on every run, so only `ah_check` findings define what is left. Fix ledger findings; treat review comments as candidates for promotion (`ah_triage` marks the ones a rule already covers, `ah_rule_propose` drafts a rule for a recurring one, and the author accepts it); never run a free review again only to check that fixes worked.
- Info-level findings (`NUM-001`, `ACR-*`, `FMT-*`, `RUB-*`) are optional hints. Never reword a number away, drop a specific example, or merge sentences to quiet one: that changes what the paper claims. Bind a number to a `\fact{id}` or leave it and tell the author.
- When the user asks for a deep review or a free-form review, call the `deep_review` tool (give `path` for one section). Do not stand in with your own reading; if you think it is the wrong tool for the scope, say so and ask. To see what the checks already cover, call `ah_triage` with `source=deep_review` and the key the review printed; do not import the report with `ah_review`, which drops each comment's quote.
- You cannot waive findings, approve briefs or plans, accept or reject fact proposals or proposed rules, verify claims, decline a review item, fill provenance, or approve a disclosure. Call `ah_decision_request` and stop. If the human explicitly asked in this message, `ah_author` (Claude Code will ask them to confirm).
- New project: `ah_profile` then `ah_init`. Existing LaTeX tree: `ah_migrate` (dry-run first; `apply` needs `confirm`). Reviewer comments: `ah_review` `import` then `ah-revise-from-review`. AI-use statement: `ah_disclosure` (author approves).

A workspace without `ah.yaml` is ordinary Academic Harness: these tools return a clear "not a project" error and the interceptors do nothing.
